name: Volcanoes and Forests of Mount Pelée and the Pitons of Northern Martinique
description: Mount Pelée is an active volcano at the northern tip of Martinique, in the Caribbean, protected together with the nearby jagged Pitons du Carbet. Its eruption on 8 May 1902 wiped out the town of Saint-Pierre in minutes and killed around 30,000 people. Today, forests climb from the seashore to the summits, sheltering rare endemic species like the Martinique volcano frog and the Martinique oriole.
